login.title: Log in
login.totpHint: Enter the 6-digit code from your authenticator app.
login.recoveryHint: Enter one of your recovery codes. Each code works only once.

password.title: Change password
password.intro: Change the password of your account in the domain. You don't need to log in to dcdash for this, and it also works if your password has expired or must be changed.
password.success: Your password was changed. Use the new password from now on, also on your other devices.
password.none: No domain offers the password change here.

policy.title: The domain's password rules
policy.minLength: At least one character | At least {n} characters
policy.complexity: Three of these four: upper case letters, lower case letters, digits, other characters; not your account or display name
policy.history: Not the same as your last password | Not the same as one of your last {n} passwords
policy.minAge: Can be changed again after an hour at the earliest | Can be changed again after {n} hours at the earliest

errors.invalid_credentials: The user name or the current password is wrong.
errors.same_password: The new password must differ from the current one.
errors.too_many_attempts: Too many failed attempts. Please wait a few minutes and try again.

errors.password_policy_tooShort: The new password is too short.
errors.password_policy_history: You used the new password before. Please choose another one.
errors.password_policy_tooYoung: Your password was changed only recently and can't be changed again yet.

errors.password_policy_policy: The new password doesn't meet the domain's rules: it may be too short, too simple, or used before.
errors.rejected: The domain rejected the change. Please contact your administrator.

enroll.title: Set up an authenticator app
enroll.introRequired: Your account requires a second login step. Set up an authenticator app now.
enroll.introVoluntary: Protect your account with a second login step.
enroll.step1: Scan the QR code with an authenticator app (for example on your phone).
enroll.step2: Enter the 6-digit code the app shows to confirm.
enroll.qrLabel: QR code for the authenticator app
enroll.manual: Can't scan? Show the key for manual entry
enroll.done: The authenticator app is set up.

recovery.intro: Store these recovery codes in a safe place. If you lose your device, each code lets you log in once. They are shown only now.

account.title: My account
account.totpOptional: Your roles don't require it, but you can set it up to protect your account. Once set up, it is required at every login.
account.regenerateHint: Enter a current code from your authenticator app. Your old recovery codes stop working.

audit.actionHint: Exact, or a prefix ending with * (for example auth.*)

sessions.terminateText: Terminate this session of {user}? The user has to log in again.

sessions.terminateAll: Terminate all sessions of this user
sessions.terminatedCount: No sessions were active. | One session was terminated. | {n} sessions were terminated.
sessions.resetTotpHint: For users who lost their device and their recovery codes. Directory users set up a new app at their next login; the break-glass account must be set up on the server.
sessions.resetTotpText: Reset the authenticator app of {user}? The user's recovery codes stop working as well, and all their sessions end.
sessions.resetDone: The authenticator app of {user} was reset.

create.title: Create a virtual machine or container
create.kind: What do you want to create?

kinds.iso: Virtual machine from an ISO image

kindHints.clone: Copies a prepared template. With cloud-init, the network and login are set up at the first start.
kindHints.iso: An empty virtual machine that starts the installation from the ISO image.
kindHints.lxc: A container from a container template.

create.fullCloneHint: A full clone is independent of the template. A linked clone is created faster and uses less space, but needs the template.
create.hostnameHint: Also the host name: letters, digits and hyphens, e.g. web-01
create.vmidRange: Empty: the next free ID. Allowed: {ranges}
create.memoryHint: For example 2048 for 2 GiB; at most {max} MiB
create.diskCloneHint: Empty: the size of the template. A larger value grows the disk; at most {max} GiB
create.linkedStorage: A linked clone uses the storage of the template.
create.netboxVlanUnknown: This VLAN is not in NetBox.
create.netboxFree: Use the free address {address} from NetBox
create.isoNetworkHint: You configure the network during the installation.
create.cloudInitHint: These settings take effect through cloud-init if the template supports it.
create.nameserversHint: Up to 3 IP addresses, separated by spaces
create.userHint: Empty: the default user of the template
create.sshKeysHint: One key per line, e.g. ssh-ed25519 AAAA… user{'@'}host
create.tagsHint: Optional, separated by spaces: lower-case letters, digits, '-', '_', '+' and '.'
create.poolHint: The new guest is added to the Proxmox pool {pool}.
create.failed: The creation failed. Steps that were done are not undone; check the guest in Proxmox and delete it if necessary.

errors.name: Letters, digits and hyphens, e.g. web-01.
errors.vmid: An ID in the allowed range.
errors.disk: Between 1 and {disk} GiB, and not smaller than the template.
errors.ipv4: An IPv4 address with prefix length, e.g. 192.0.2.10/24.
errors.ipv6: An IPv6 address with prefix length, e.g. 2001:db8::10/64.
errors.login: Set a password or SSH keys for root.
errors.sshKeys: One public key per line in OpenSSH format.
errors.mac: A unicast MAC address like BC:24:11:12:34:56.
errors.macTwice: This MAC address is used twice.

create.macHint: Generated; change it only if the guest needs a specific address.
create.dhcpHint: Reservations are made for the MAC address of a network device and added after the guest was created, before it starts. DHCPv6 servers have to accept the MAC address as identifier (host-reservation-identifiers with hw-address). This step is optional.
create.reservedAddressHint: Empty: only the host name is reserved.
create.dnsHint: Records are added after the guest was created, before it starts. A PTR record needs the reverse zone of the address. This step is optional.
create.recordNameHint: Relative to the zone, {'@'} for the zone itself, or fully qualified with a trailing dot.

delete.purge: Also remove it from backup jobs, replication and high availability
delete.purgeHint: Otherwise these keep referring to the deleted ID.
delete.stopFirst: Stop the guest to delete it.

hints.grow: Disks can only grow. Leave empty to keep the size.

hints.macKept: The MAC address stays when a device is changed.

hardware.pendingHint: Some changes are pending. They take effect when the VM is started again: after a stop and start, or a reboot through Proxmox, but not after a reboot from inside the guest.
hardware.runningHint: The VM is running. Changes that Proxmox can’t apply to a running VM stay pending until the VM is started again.
hardware.notConfigurable: Changes are not possible: this cluster has no provisioning settings.
hardware.detachText: Detach {disk} ({volume})? The disk stays as an unused disk of the VM and can be attached again.
hardware.deleteDiskText: The disk {disk} ({volume}) and all its data will be destroyed. This can’t be undone.
hardware.deleteRunning: Stop the VM or detach the disk first.
hardware.removeNetworkText: Remove {net} ({mac})? The guest loses this network connection.

health.restartText: The service is restarted on {firewall}. It is briefly unavailable.

aliases.name: Name
aliases.deleteText: The alias is deleted and the packet filter reloaded. OPNsense refuses aliases that rules use.
aliases.nameHint: Up to 32 letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter or underscore
aliases.contentHint: One entry per line: addresses, networks, ports, URLs or other aliases, depending on the type.
aliases.appliedHint: The change is loaded into the packet filter immediately.

rules.netHint: any, an address, a network, an alias, or an interface network such as lan
rules.portHint: A port, a range such as 1000-2000, or a port alias
rules.deleteText: The rule {rule} is deleted with a savepoint.
rules.savepointHint: dcdash applies every change with a savepoint and then checks that it can still reach the firewall. If not, OPNsense restores the previous rules within a minute.
rules.noSavepoint: This OPNsense version has no savepoints (removed in 26.7), so nothing undoes a rule that cuts dcdash off. dcdash therefore doesn't change the rules of the interface it reaches the firewall through ({interfaces}), floating rules, or rules on interface groups.
rules.guardUnknown: This OPNsense version has no savepoints, and dcdash can't tell which interface it reaches the firewall through, so it doesn't change rules here. Name the interface with protected_interfaces in the configuration. ({error})
rules.lockedOut: After the change, dcdash could not reach {firewall}. Without savepoints, nothing undoes the change: check the rules in the firewall's web interface.
rules.rolledBack: After the change, dcdash could not reach {firewall}. OPNsense restores the previous rules within a minute.
